先生，
    1941年3月15日凌晨12时15分，接到第二外事科P.3.640号警员Kasai的电话报告，称外白渡桥上一名上海志愿军（S.V.C.）哨兵与一名日本人发生纠纷。副督察长Hillhouse和副督察Matsushita随即前往现场，获悉事发原因为外白渡桥西南侧执勤的上海志愿军（S.V.C.）哨兵与居住于四川北路117号英安里、受雇于中国海关的日本籍职员F.Noguchi之间发生争执。后者身着制服，由同样受雇于中国海关的日本籍职员S.Mikawa（住址：南京路70弄15号）陪同。

(Hongkew) and F.P.S.640 Sakasai(Hongkew) were at the
South end of the bridge near Soochow Road corner at
the time of the actual altercation and did not observe
the sentry striking F.Noguchi with his rifle,but on
pages.zh:
第2页

步枪。后者随即用步枪击打其右肩，枪身某部分擦伤其耳垂，造成轻微割伤。据哨兵称，F.Noguchi仍试图通过，于是他便将装有刺刀的步枪指向其身体。F.Noguchi在向前挤压时，两次触碰到刺刀尖，刺破了其衣物。此事发生后，F.Noguchi穿过马路，走到桥顶，据观察他与那里执勤的日本哨兵交谈。二等兵Johnson立即摇响通往警卫室的铃，下士Filipovitch随即赶到。当他到达哨所时，F.Noguchi返回，并试图说服下士Filipovitch陪他到桥北侧，期间曾拉扯其上衣。下士Filipovitch予以拒绝，随后F.Noguchi及其未参与争执的同伴向北穿过大桥。

    当时，实际争执发生时，中央区的F.P.S.179号警员Geisler、虹口区的F.P.S.183号警员Farly以及虹口区的F.P.S.640号警员Sakasai正在靠近苏州路路口的大桥南端，并未目睹哨兵用步枪击打F.Noguchi，但在

pages.en:
Page 3

arriving at the scene they observed that the latter's
right ear was bleeding slightly. P.P.S.Perly also
saw F.Noguchi talking with Corporal Filipovitch
and lay hold of the latter's tunic.
    While the undersigned was at the scene,Sub.
Lieutenant Mokuyama,Japanese Naval Landing Party,
arrived and made enquiries,later returning to the
North side of the bridge,stating that he would later
submit a report to his superiors.
    Officers of the American Company S.V.C. also
attended and conducted enquiries.
    It was learned that F.Noguchi and his companion
had proceeded to the Naval Landing Party Sub Station
on Tiendong Rd. D.S.Matsushita visited there and they
accompanied him to this station. When questioned
F.Noguchi stated that he and S.Mikawa were proceeding
over the Garden Bridge on their way home when they
were stopped by the S.V.C.sentry who instructed them
to walk on the footpath. He remonstrated and stated
that he came home the same way every night and had
always walked on the roadway without being stopped.
According to him the sentry then struck him a blow on
the neck with his rifle and on being asked the reason,
prodded him three times on the chest with the point of
the bayonet. He stated that following this incident
pages.zh:
第3页

抵达现场时，他们观察到后者右耳有轻微出血。P.P.S.Perly也看到F.Noguchi与下士Filipovitch交谈，并抓住后者的上衣。
    当署名人在现场时，日本海军陆战队少尉Mokuyama抵达并进行询问，随后返回桥北侧，称稍后将向其上级提交报告。
    上海志愿军（S.V.C.）美国连的军官也到场并进行了调查。
    获悉F.Noguchi及其同伴已前往天通庵路的日本海军陆战队分站。副督察Matsushita前往该处，他们随同他来到本局。在接受询问时，F.Noguchi称，他和S.Mikawa在回家途中经过外白渡桥时，被上海志愿军（S.V.C.）哨兵拦下，指令他们走人行道。他提出抗议并称，他每晚都走同一条路回家，一直走在马路上且从未被拦下。据他称，哨兵随后用步枪击打其颈部，并在被问及原因时，用刺刀尖捅了其胸部三次。他称在此事之后

pages.en:
page 4

he observed several foreigners passing on the roadway
and returned to ask the sentry why Japanese were
stopped and foreigners allowed to go. He and S.Kikawa
then proceeded to the Naval Landing Party Sub Station
and submitted a report. The foregoing was corroborated
by S.Kikawa and both wrote statements, translations of
which are attached. F.Noguchi showed small holes in
the right and left breast pockets of his tunic and
stated that these were caused by the point of the
bayonet which however did not pierce his skin.
When he first came to the station he informed
the undersigned that he did not wish to attend
hospital, but afterwards stated he wished to do so.
He was sent to the Foo King Hospital accompanied
by Y.P.S.753(Section 2) and after treatment, was
allowed to go home. The following medical certificate
was issued "Contused wound on right ear".
Officer i/c informed.

他看到几名外国人从马路上走过，便回去问哨兵为何拦住日本人却允许外国人通过。他和S.Kikawa随后前往日本海军陆战队分站并提交了一份报告。上述情况得到S.Kikawa的证实，两人均写了陈述书，译文附后。F.Noguchi展示了其上衣左右胸袋上的小孔，并称这些是由刺刀尖造成的，但并未刺破皮肤。他初到警局时告知署名人他不希望去医院，但随后表示希望去。他在Y.P.S.753号警员（第二科）的陪同下被送往福金医院，经治疗后获准回家。出具了以下医疗证明：“右耳挫伤”。

At 11.45p.m. 14/3/41, I was passing by the American

in force I cannot understand why Japanese are stopped from

I wish to protest against the sentry's actions as I did not

pages.en:
At 11.56a.m. 4/12/40 a telephone message
was received from C.C.R. reporting an armed
robbery in progress at 321 Kiangse Rd. the
station alarm was rung and all available men
under C.I. Brownrigg,C.I.Telfer and D.I.Moir
went to the scene,but on arrival found it to be
a case of assault.
Enquiries by D.S. Cooke,D.S.I. Kobayashi
and C.D.C.203 revealed the following:-
At about 11.30a.m. 4/12/40 F.S. 13 McCahey
in civilian clothes was walking west on Peking
Rd. near Kiangse Rd. when his attention was drawn
to a large crowd of Chinese who had congregated
on the north-west corner of the above intersection,
and C.P.C. 1426,Central,walking towards the crowd.
On getting nearer he observed a male Chinese lying
on the roadway beside a public-ricksha,and a male
Japanese turn round on the C.P.C. and catch hold
of his tunic collar with his left hand and
strike him on the body with his right clenched fist.
It was then that F.S.McCahey intervened with the
object of preventing further trouble. He tried to
persuade the Japanese to desist,but owing to
language difficulties this was apparently not
understood, He then decided to bring all concerned
to the station. The Japanese by this time was in a
excited state of mind,shouting and struggling to free
himself.
On the way to the station,via Kiangse Rd.
pages.zh:
1940年12月4日上午11时56分，接到中央无线电室电话报告，称江西路321号正在发生持械抢劫。警局警报响起，所有可用人员在首席督察Brownrigg、首席督察Telfer和侦探督察Moir的带领下前往现场，但到达后发现是一起袭击案件。
经副督察Cooke、副督察长Kobayashi和C.D.C.203号警员调查，查明情况如下：
1940年12月4日上午11时30分左右，便衣外国警员F.S. 13 McCahey在北京路近江西路处向西行走时，注意到一大群中国人聚集在上述交叉路口的西北角，中央巡捕房警员C.P.C. 1426正走向人群。走近后，他看到一名中国男子躺在马路上一辆公共人力车旁，一名日本男子转身面向该警员，左手抓住其上衣领口，右手握拳击打其身体。此时F.S.McCahey介入以防止事态进一步恶化。他试图劝止该日本人，但由于语言障碍，对方显然未能理解。随后他决定将所有相关人员带回警局。此时该日本人情绪激动，叫喊并挣扎试图逃脱。
在经由江西路前往警局的途中，

pages.en:
Page 3

F.S.McCobey deemed it advisable to phone to the
station for a m/car, to take them all in, as the large
crowd of Chinese, who were following behind began
to adopt a very hostile attitude towards the Japanese,
and with this object in view he entered an exchange
shop on the corner of Kiangse and Tientsin Rds.
(531 Kiangse Rd.) and telephoned to Central Station
for a m/car, which arrived about five minutes later, and
conveyed him and the Japanese to the station.

Enquiries at the station, and from statements taken,
the following is revealed as having led up to the
assault.

The accused, Masao Kimura, Korean, age 27, S/Merchant,
residing 57, Kung Ping Lee, Kungping Rd. stated that at
about 11.10a.m. 4/12/40 he engaged a public ricsha on
Nanking Rd. near the Race Course, to take him to Szechuen
Rd. Bridge, on arriving near to 831 Kiangse Rd. he saw a
male Chinese whom he suspected of being responsible for
a theft of clothing, value $1,200, from his home on
24/11/40 (Wayside P.I.R. 2377/40). He ordered the ricsha
coolie to go faster with the idea of overtaking the
suspect. However the coolie did not obey him and stopped
the ricsha, he got out and he and the coolie started to
fight together. A C.P.C., number unknown, then came on the
pages.zh:
第3页

F.S.McCobey认为最好打电话给警局叫一辆机动车，将他们全部带走，因为跟随在后的大群中国人开始对这名日本人表现出非常敌对的态度。为此目的，他进入江西路与天津路路口的一家兑换店（江西路531号），致电中央巡捕房要求派机动车，该车约五分钟后到达，将他及该日本人送往警局。

通过在警局的调查及取得的陈述，揭示了导致此次袭击的前因如下。

被告Masao Kimura，朝鲜人，27岁，单身/商人，居住于公平路57号康平里。他陈述称，1940年12月4日上午11时10分左右，他在南京路近跑马厅处雇佣了一辆公共人力车，前往四川路桥。当到达江西路831号附近时，他看到一名中国男子，怀疑此人应对1940年11月24日其家中发生的价值1,200美元的衣物盗窃案负责（路边巡逻调查报告 2377/40）。他命令人力车夫加快车速，意图追上嫌疑人。然而车夫没有听从他的命令并停下了人力车，他下车后与车夫扭打起来。随后一名编号不详的中央巡捕房警员（C.P.C.）来到

pages.en:
Page 4

scene and caught hold of his necktie,this further
annoyed him so he started fighting with the C.P.C.
A foreigner in plain clothes then came up and
knocked him down. He was later taken into an exchange
shop,where he was held by three C.P.C.s while the
foreigner struck him three times,which made the Chinese
crowd laugh. He was later taken to the Police station.
The injured ricsha coolie is one named Tseu
Tsing Yuen(          )badge No. 12068,residing 17 An Yoeh
Li,Rue Conty F.C. was removed to the Lester Chinese
Hospital,from where a doctor's chit was issued:-
" Simple fracture of Rt. femur.Not likely to be serious.
30-40 days' treatment in Hospital."
From his statement it will be seen,that at
about 11.45a.m. 4/12/40,he was pulling his public
ricsha,Lic.No.7226,on Foochow Rd. near Hupeh Rd. when
he was engaged by a Japanese,who instructed him to go to
Szechuen Rd. Bridge,offering a fare of 20 cents,which he
accepted. When he was pulling his passenger on Szechuen
Rd. near Peking Rd. he told him to turn west along
Peking Rd. but he informed him that Szechuen Rd. Bridge was
straight in front. However the passenger insisted,so he
complied with his wishes,on arriving at the intersection
of Peking & Kiangsu Rds.,the Japanese got out of his
pages.zh:
第4页

现场并抓住他的领带，这使他更加恼怒，于是他开始与该警员打斗。随后一名便衣外国人上前将其打倒。他后来被带进一家兑换店，在那里他被三名中央巡捕房警员按住，而那名外国人打了他三拳，引得围观的中国人群发笑。他随后被带到警察局。
受伤的人力车夫名为Tseu Tsing Yuen（          ），徽章编号12068，居住于法租界康悌路17号安业里（An Yoeh Li），被送往莱斯中国医院，医生出具了以下纸条：
“右股骨简单骨折。可能不严重。需住院治疗30-40天。”
从其陈述中可以看出，1940年12月4日上午11时45分左右，他拉着牌照号为7226的公共人力车，在福州路近湖北路处，被一名日本人雇用，该日本人指令他去四川路桥，车费20角，他接受了。当他在北京路近四川路处拉着乘客时，他告诉乘客沿北京路向西转，但他告知乘客四川路桥就在正前方。然而乘客坚持己见，于是他顺从了乘客的愿望，到达北京路与江苏路交叉路口时，该日本人下车

pages.en:
Page 5

ricsha and assaulted him by hitting him with his
clenched fists and kicking him on the right leg
which was broken. Chinese policeman then came on
the scene, and tried to persuade the Japanese to stop, but
he tried to take the policeman's pistol away from
him. Shortly afterwards a foreigner came on the
scene and caught hold of the Japanese, who was then
sent to the police station. He was removed to the
Lester Chinese Hospital.

From C.P.C. 1436's statement it will be seen
that at about 11.50a.m. 4/12/49 he was on duty at the
Kiangse-Pekin Rds intersection, his attention was drawn
to a quarrel between a Japanese, dressed in civilian
clothes and a public ric sha coolie. He then saw the
Japanese assault the coolie, he appeared to be wrestling
with him. When the coolie fell to the ground with a
broken leg, he continued to assault him. The C.P.C.
approached with the idea of persuading the Japanese
to desist, he attempted to take his pistol away from
him, tore his uniform and tore his white traffic sleeve
from his arm. F.S. 13 then arrived on the scene,
dressed in civilian clothes, and assisted the C.P.C. to
take the Japanese to the station.

The accused was handed over to the Japanese
Consular Police at 2.15p.m. by D.P.S. Yamahara. He has
pages.zh:
第5页

人力车并殴打他，用紧握的拳头击打并踢其右腿，导致骨折。随后一名中国巡捕赶到现场，试图劝止该日本人，但该日本人试图夺走巡捕的手枪。不久后，一名外国人赶到现场并抓住了该日本人，随后将其送往警察局。他被送往莱斯华民医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）。

从华捕警长（C.P.C.）1436号的陈述中可以看出，1940年12月4日上午11时50分左右，他在江西路与北京路路口执勤，注意到一名身穿便服的日本人与一名公共人力车夫发生争吵。随后他看到该日本人袭击车夫，两人似乎在扭打。当车夫腿部骨折倒地后，该日本人继续对其进行殴打。华捕警长上前试图劝止该日本人停止施暴，但该日本人试图夺走他的手枪，撕破了他的制服，并扯下了他手臂上的白色交通袖标。随后外勤警员（F.S.）13号身着便服赶到现场，协助华捕警长将该日本人带往警局。

被告于下午2时15分由日籍副巡官（D.P.S.）山原（Yamahara）移交给日本领事警察。他已被

pages.en:
Page 6

been charged and will appear before the Japanese
Consular Court at a.m. 6/12/40.
    A charge relative to assault on Police will be

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of F.S. 13 McCahey
native of taken by me.
at Central on the 4.12.40. and interpreted by.

At 11.30a.m. 4/12/40 whilst off duty I was walking west on
Peking Road in civilian clothes, on approaching Kiangse Road, I
observed a crowd of Chinese gathered at the North-west corner of
the intersection, at the same time C.P.C. 1436 on traffic duty
at the above intersection left his post and walked towards the
crowd to see what the trouble was.

But on his arrival a Japanese in civilian dress, who had
apparently assaulted a ricsha coolie, suddenly turned round on
the C.P.C. and caught hold of him by the tunic neck with his left
hand and commenced to assault him about the body with his right
clenched fist.

At this time the undersigned arrived on the scene, saw the
ricsha coolie lying on the roadway beside his public ricsha,
apparently in pain, I requested the Japanese to stop, but as he
was very excited he would not listen to me, so I caught hold of
him by the right arm and held him, but he still refused to let
the C.P.C. free.

At this time the bystanders commenced to kick the Japanese,
so for his safety, and owing to language difficulties I decided
to bring all concerned to the station.

On the way along Kiangse Road the crowd became more abusive
so I took the Japanese into an exchange shop at the corner of
Kiangse and Tientsin Roads, where I phoned Central Station for
a motor car, which arrived in a matter of a few minutes, when
we brought the Japanese to the station.

The ricsha coolie was taken to the Lester Chinese Hospital,
where he is detained.

〔签名〕
F.S. 13 McCahey.

以下为外勤警员（F.S.）13号麦卡希（McCahey）的陈述，由本人于1940年12月4日在中央捕房录取，并由……翻译。

1940年12月4日上午11时30分，我下班后身着便服沿北京路向西行走，接近江西路时，我观察到路口西北角聚集了一群中国人，与此同时，在上述路口执行交通任务的华捕警长（C.P.C.）1436号离开岗位，走向人群查看发生了什么事。

但当他到达时，一名显然刚袭击过人力车夫的便服日本人突然转身面向华捕警长，左手抓住其制服领口，右手握拳开始殴打其身体部位。

此时本人抵达现场，看到人力车夫躺在路边他的人力车旁，显然很痛苦，我要求该日本人住手，但他情绪非常激动，不听劝阻，于是我抓住他的右臂并将其控制住，但他仍拒绝放开华捕警长。

此时旁观者开始踢打该日本人，为了他的安全，也由于语言障碍，我决定将所有相关人员带往警局。

在沿江西路行进途中，人群变得更加辱骂不止，因此我将该日本人带入江西路与天津路路口的一家兑换店，在那里我打电话给中央捕房请求派车，几分钟后车辆到达，我们将该日本人带往警局。

人力车夫被送往莱斯华民医院（Lester Chinese Hospital），目前留院治疗。

〔签名〕
外勤警员（F.S.）13号 麦卡希（McCahey）。

Tseu Tsing Yuen

Tseu Tsing Yuen,22,Kompo,public ricsha coolie,
badge No. 12068,residing at 17 An Yoh Lee,Sue Conty,F.C.
At about 11.45a.m. 4/12/4C,whilst pulling my ricsha
Lic.No.7226 on Foochow near Hupeh Rd.,a Japanese instructed
me to take him to Szechuen Road Bridge,he offering 20¢
for my fare. When I was pulling him in my ricsha on
Szechuen Road near Peking Road,I was instructed by him
to proceed west. I told him that the Szechuen Rd. Bridge
was not far in front so why should I proceed west. However
he insisted that I had to go to west which I did. On
arriving at the intersection of Peking - Kiangse roads,the
Japanese alighted from my ricsha and assaulted me by striking
me with his clenched fists and kicking me with his foot,
which resulted in my right leg being fractured. I fell to
the ground. A Chinese contable then came who intended to
persuade the Japanese not to assault me but the Japanese
tried to seize the service weapon from the constable. Shortly
afterwards,a foreigner came to the scene and got hold of the
Japanese. The Japanese was then escorted to the Police
Station while I was sent to the Lester Chinese Hospital. I wish
to prefer a charge against the Japanese. The above is my
true statement.

Signed.

徐清元（Tseu Tsing Yuen），22岁，江苏人（Kompo），公共人力车夫，徽章号12068，居住于法租界苏省安义里17号。
1940年12月4日上午11时45分左右，当我拉着牌照号为7226的人力车在福州路近湖北路处行驶时，一名日本人指令我将他拉至四川路桥，出价车费20分。当我拉着他在四川路近北京路处行驶时，他指令我向西行。我告诉他四川路桥就在前方不远处，为何要向西行。然而他坚持要我向西行，我便照做了。到达北京路与江西路路口时，该日本人从我的车上下来，用紧握的拳头击打并用脚踢我，导致我右腿骨折。我倒在地上。随后一名中国巡捕前来，意图劝止该日本人不要殴打我，但该日本人试图夺取巡捕的佩枪。不久后，一名外国人来到现场并抓住了该日本人。该日本人随后被护送至警察局，而我被送往莱斯华民医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）。我希望对该日本人提出控告。以上是我的真实陈述。

签名。

At about 6.30 p.m. 28-3-40 P.P.J. 146

CHINA PRESS

King Assault
Case Will Be
Heard Here

Denying that the four Japanese subjects, two Japanese and two Formosans, who attacked S.M.P. Sergeant M. King Wednesday night on Nanking Road had been discharged by the Japanese Consular Police, the Shanghai Municipal Police said that the official report was the result of a misunderstanding.

The four men were released on their own security Thursday morning, after they had been handed over to the Japanese Consular Police by Louza Police Station.

The Japanese Consular Police, it was revealed yesterday, have asked the S.M.P. for written evidence, and the case will be heard when Sgt. King, and the two foreigners who came to his assistance, Pte. Stevens of the Seaforth Highlanders and Mr. R. MacNeil, P.W.D. inspector, will be able to appear in the Japanese Consular Court.

The four Japanese subjects, it was stated, will be charged with assaulting a police officer in the course of his duty.

Sgt. King was assaulted when the quartet attempted to protect several prostitutes whom Sgt. King, on duty in plainclothes, attempted to clear from Nanking Road, near Chekiang Road. In the course of the scuffle Sgt. King was seriously injured and transported to the Country Hospital, from which he was dismissed Friday morning.

altercation with Sergeant M. King of
the Shanghai Municipal Police on
Nanking Road Wednesday evening.
Foreign press reports that the case
had been "remanded until a future
date" when the injured police ser-
geant would be able to appear before
the Japanese Consular Court were
derided by the Information Bureau
of the Japanese Consulate-General
yesterday.
According to the deposition taken
by the Japanese Consular Police, Ser-
geant King is alleged to have pushed
one of the four Japanese subjects off
the footpath, shouting "Get out".
When the Japanese remonstrated,
the police sergeant was alleged to
have said "You Jap", whereupon the
Japanese wanted to accompany the
sergeant to an S.M.P. station to lodge
a complaint. Sergeant King, at the
time, was in civilian clothes and car-
ried no mark identifying him as a
police officer on duty, it was pointed
out.
Taken to the Louza Police station,
where no Japanese officers of the
S.M.P. are stationed, the Japanese
claimed that they were denied the
use of the telephone to communicate
with the Japanese Consulate-General.
In releasing the four men, the
Japanese consular police, however,
cautioned them against becoming in-
volved in street brawls, a consular
spokesman said.

袭击者被
日本人释放

四名被控袭击金（King）巡长的男子
被判无罪

周四，日本领事警察当局释放了四名日本臣民，他们于周三晚上在南京路与上海公共租界工部局警务处的M. 金巡长发生冲突。昨日，日本总领事馆情报局嘲笑了外国媒体关于该案已“延期审理”，待受伤警长能够出庭日本领事法庭时再行审理的报道。

根据日本领事警察取得的证词，据称金巡长将四名日本臣民中的一人推离人行道，并大喊“滚开”。当日本人提出抗议时，据称该警长说道“你这日本佬”，随后日本人希望陪同警长前往工部局警务处派出所提出投诉。有人指出，当时金巡长身着便衣，且未佩戴任何表明其正在执行警务的标识。

日本人被带往老闸捕房，那里没有工部局警务处的日本警官驻守，他们声称被拒绝使用电话与日本总领事馆联系。然而，一位领事发言人表示，日本领事警察在释放这四名男子时，警告他们不要卷入街头斗殴。

DEC 16 1939

Officials Are
Bewildered By
Court Action

High officials of the S.M.P.
were bewildered yesterday by an
announcement from Japanese
Consular Police authorities that
the four Japanese subjects who
were involved in a clash with
Sergeant M. King of the S.M.P.
Wednesday evening were dis-
charged the next day.

Reports which appeared yester-
day in English-language papers
that the case had been remanded
to a future date, when the injured
police sergeant would be able to
appear before the Japanese Con-
sular Court, were denied by the
Information Bureau of the Japan-
ese Consulate-General yesterday.

The incident occurred shortly
before 7:30 p.m. Wednesday on
Nanking Road, near Chekiang
Road, when the four Japanese
attempted to interfere with Ser-
geant King, on duty in plainclothes,
who was attempting to clear the
street of undesirable women.

Defend Prostitutes

The four Japanese, together
with a fifth who subsequently
attempted to act as a peace-
maker, attempted to defend the
prostitutes. When Sergeant
King made it clear that he
would act according to his
orders, the four Japanese leapt
at him, beating him with feet
and fists.

Sergeant King received severe
stomach injuries.

The four Japanese attempted
to drag the officer into a taxi,
from a Hongkew garage, which
was awaiting them, but were
prevented from doing so by the
intervention of Private Stevens,
of the Seaforth Highlanders,
and Mr. R. MacNeil, inspector
of the S.M.C. Public Works
Department.

The four Japanese were ar-
rested, detained overnight at the
Louza Station, and turned over
to the Japanese Consular Police
Thursday morning.

Police Amazed

Yesterday's announcement that
the four Japanese had been dis-
charged with merely a warning
against "becoming involved in street
brawls" was greeted with amaze-
ment by S.M.P. officials, who pre-
viously told the press that the
Japanese authorities were taking a
serious view of the matter.

Japanese allege that Sgt. King
pushed one of the Japanese off the
pavement, and later shouted "You
Jap!" at him.

It was also alleged that the four
Japanese were refused permission
to communicate with the Japanese
Consulate-General at Louza Police
Station.

1939年12月16日

官员对
法院行动
感到困惑

昨日，日本领事警察当局宣布，周三晚上与工部局警务处M. 金巡长发生冲突的四名日本臣民已于次日被释放，工部局警务处的高级官员对此感到困惑。

昨日英文报纸刊登报道称，该案已延期至未来某日审理，届时受伤的警长将能够出庭日本领事法庭，日本总领事馆情报局昨日否认了这一报道。

事件发生在周三晚上7点30分前不久，地点位于南京路靠近浙江路处，当时这四名日本人试图干涉正在便衣执勤的金巡长，后者正试图清理街道上的不良妇女。

为妓女辩护

这四名日本人，连同随后试图充当和事佬的第五人，试图保护这些妓女。当金巡长明确表示他将按照命令行事时，这四名日本人扑向他，用脚和拳头殴打他。

金巡长腹部受到重伤。

这四名日本人试图将该警官拖进一辆来自虹口车库、正在等候他们的出租车，但这一企图因海福斯高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）的史蒂文斯（Stevens）列兵和工部局工务处督察R. 麦克尼尔（MacNeil）先生的干预而未能得逞。

这四名日本人被捕，在老闸捕房拘留过夜，并于周四上午移交给日本领事警察。

警方震惊

昨日宣布这四名日本人仅因被警告不要“卷入街头斗殴”而被释放，工部局警务处官员对此感到震惊，他们此前曾告诉媒体，日本当局正严肃看待此事。

日本人指控金巡长将其中一名日本人推离人行道，随后对其大喊“你这日本佬！”

另有人指控，这四名日本人在老闸捕房被拒绝与日本总领事馆联系。

pages.en:
December 15, 1939.

MAINICHI

BRITISH POLICEMAN ASSAULTS JAPANESE ON NANKING
ROAD

At about 7.20 p.m. December 13
two Japanese named T. Yamada, age 26, residing on
North Szechuen Road, and S. Okuno, 29, residing on
Yuen Chang Road, in company with two Formosan employees
arrived in front of the Sincere Department Store on
Nanking Road when a European pushed them away, shouting
to them in English, "Get away". Mr. Okuno replied
in English, "We are Japanese. What is the matter with
you?". Mr. Okuno then asked the European to
explain the unreasonable obstruction of his passage,
whereupon the European assaulted Mr. Okuno in the face
saying, "What are you talking about, you Jap". Mr.
Okuno then attempted to pull the European into a motor
car with a view to taking him to a Police Station where
he desired to lodge a complaint with Japanese police
officers against the unlawful action of the European,
but his attempt was frustrated by about ten Municipal
policemen who had arrived on the scene and the two
Japanese together with the two Formosans were taken
to Louza Station where no Japanese policemen are
attached.

At the Station Mr. Okuno asked
the police for permission to use the telephone to
communicate with the Japanese Consular Police but his
request was rejected. Afterwards Detective Sub-
Inspector Kobayashi of Central Police Station arrived
at the Station and communicated with the Japanese
Consular Police to whom the Japanese were later handed
over. At this time it was first learned that the
European who was involved in the trouble was a police
officer. Mr. Okuno expressed his regret for having
made trouble with the Police but he was highly indignant
over the European policeman's unlawful action.

The explanation advanced by the
S.M.P. is that Probationary Sergeant King, the European
involved in the case, in company with two Chinese
constables was engaged in dispersing street girls in
the vicinity of the Sincere Department Store and had
asked the Japanese to go away. Thus, the trouble was
started.

As it was then only 7.20 p.m. no
man in his senses can believe that the Police were
dispersing street girls at that time. If Probationary
Sergeant King was actually engaged in this work at
such a time it would be an exposure of his gross stupidity
in the execution of his police duty.

1939年12月15日。

《每日新闻》

英国警察在南京路
袭击日本人

12月13日晚上约7点20分，两名居住在四川北路、26岁的山田T.（T. Yamada）和居住在源昌路、29岁的奥野S.（S. Okuno），与两名台湾雇员一同抵达南京路先施公司百货商店前，此时一名欧洲人将他们推开，并用英语对他们喊道：“走开”。奥野先生用英语回答：“我们是日本人。你有什么问题？”。随后，奥野先生要求该欧洲人解释为何无理阻碍其通行，该欧洲人随即击打奥野先生的面部，说道：“你在说什么，你这日本佬”。奥野先生随后试图将该欧洲人拉进一辆汽车，打算将其带到警察局，向日本警官投诉该欧洲人的非法行为，但其企图被大约十名赶到现场的公共租界警察挫败，这两名日本人连同两名台湾人被带往老闸捕房，那里没有配备日本警察。

在捕房，奥野先生请求警察允许使用电话与日本领事警察联系，但其请求被拒绝。随后，中央捕房的侦探副督察小林（Kobayashi）到达捕房，并与日本领事警察取得联系，日本人随后被移交给他们。此时才首次得知卷入纠纷的欧洲人是一名警官。奥野先生对给警察带来麻烦表示遗憾，但他对该欧洲警察的非法行为感到极为愤慨。

工部局警务处提出的解释是，卷入此案的欧洲人、见习巡长金（King），与两名华籍警员一起，在先施公司百货商店附近驱散街头妓女，并要求日本人离开。因此引发了纠纷。

当时仅为晚上7点20分，任何理智的人都不会相信警察会在那个时间驱散街头妓女。如果见习巡长金确实在那个时间从事这项工作，那将暴露出他在执行警务职责时的极度愚蠢。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

（批：8-07 / 4 12 39）

Japanese Attack
Police Officer

Sergeant King Taken to
Hospital After Nanking
Road Assault

Badly beaten by a gang of about
six or seven Japanese while engaged
in the pursuit of his duty in Nanking
Road yesterday evening, Sergeant M.
King a canadian member of the
Shanghai Municipal Police, attached
to Louza Police Station, is being de-
tained in the Country Hospital suffer-
ing from shock, severe bruising and
other injuries believed to include a
broken thumb.

The assault on Sergeant King, who
was in plain clothes at the time, took
place when he had herded a group
of prostitutes into a corner to await
the arrival of the van from the sta-
tion. This was part of his regular
duty, his orders being to clear the
area of these women, who congregate
there in large numbers.

While awaiting the van, a group of
six or seven Japanese arrived at the
scene, probably from a car in the
vicinity, and commenced to push
Sergeant King. When he attempted
to drive them away, members of the
group attacked him and beat him
severely about the body.

After knocking him down, the
Japanese attempted to drag him into
a car, stating that they were going
to take him to Hongkew. Luckily
some foreigners arrived on the scene
and stopped this attempt. A few
moments later the station van arrived
and four Japanese, were taken into
custody, the rest having fled.

At the station charges were made
against three of the men, whose
descriptions had been given by Ser-
geant King who was taken to hos-
pital, and they were handed over to
the Japanese Consular Police. The
fourth man, according to Sergeant
King, had attempted to stop the others
and had helped him to protect him-
self from their blows.

（手写签名/标记：C 1/2）

《字林西报》。

（批注：8-07 / 4 12 39）

日本人袭击
警官

金巡长在南京路遇袭后
被送往医院

昨晚，加拿大籍上海公共租界工部局警务处警员、隶属老闸捕房的M. 金巡长在南京路执勤时，遭到约六七名日本人的团伙严重殴打，目前因休克、严重挫伤及其他被认为包括拇指骨折在内的伤势，留院治疗于宏恩医院（Country Hospital）。

对金巡长的袭击发生时，他身着便衣，当时他正将一群妓女赶至角落，等待警局厢式车的到来。这是他的常规职责的一部分，他的命令是清除聚集在该地区的大量此类妇女。

在等待厢式车时，一群六七名日本人可能从附近的车辆下来到达现场，并开始推搡金巡长。当他试图驱赶他们时，该团伙成员袭击了他，并对其身体进行了严重殴打。

在将他打倒后，日本人试图将他拖进一辆汽车，声称要带他去虹口。幸运的是，一些外国人赶到现场并制止了这一企图。几分钟后，警局厢式车到达，四名日本人被拘留，其余人逃逸。

在捕房，根据被送往医院的金巡长提供的描述，对其中三人提出了指控，并将他们移交给日本领事警察。据金巡长称，第四人曾试图阻止其他人，并帮助他保护自己免受殴打。

（手写签名/标记：C 1/2）

SHANGHAI TIMES.

DEC 1 4 1939

FOREIGN SERGEANT
IS ASSAULTED

Sgt. King Injured In
Scuffle With Three
Japanese

Sergeant M. King, attached to
Louza Station, was severely injur-
ed about the body as the result of
a scuffle between the police officer
and three Japanese in civilian
clothes on Nanking Road at about
7.30 yesterday evening.
The incident occurred in the
vicinity of Sincere's following a
heated argument between Sergeant
King and the three Japanese, who,
apparently, were under the influ-
ence of liquor. The policeman
was engaged in clearing the side-
walk, when, it was alleged, he was
beset and assaulted by the three
men.
Sergeant King's injuries were
such that it was found necessary
to take him to the Police Hospital
for medical attention. His assail-
ants were immediately arrested on
the spot and taken to Louza Police
Station. They were later handed
over at the request of the Japan-
ese authorities.

按照预先安排，我于 1939年12月19日下午7时05分，在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）70弄外，便衣会见了警佐 F.S. 93 King、华捕巡长 C.P.S. 1013 和华捕巡警 C.P.C. 3018（配属妓院执照科）。

CHINA PRESS.

DEC 15 1939

Japanese Charged
Assailants Of
S.M.C. Officer
To Face Court

Three Japanese import and export businessmen who were arrested Wednesday night after assaulting and causing serious injury to Sgt. M. King of the S.M.P. were handed over to the Japanese Consular Police yesterday morning and charged with assaulting a police officer.

Sgt. King, meanwhile, was recovering from the beating when four of the five Japanese set upon him as he was on duty in plain-clothes on Nanking Road clearing the main thoroughfare of undesirable women.

Angered by his arrest of several women, the five Japanese argued with the officer, and later four assaulted him while the fifth tried to pacify his friends.

Despite the pleas of the lone Japanese who did not lay hands on the officer, the other four attempted to drag him into a taxi from a Hongkew garage which was awaiting them in an effort to take Sgt. King north of Soochow Creek.

The timely intervention of Private Stevens of the Seaforth Highlanders and Mr. R. MacNeil, inspector of the S.M.C. Public Works Department, who intervened in the melee, saved Sgt. King from the infuriated Japanese.

1939年12月15日

日本人被控
袭击工部局警官
将出庭受审

周三晚袭击上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）警长 M. King 并致其重伤后被逮捕的三名日本进出口商人，于昨日上午被移交给日本领事馆警察，并被指控袭击警务人员。

与此同时，King 警长正在从殴打中恢复，当时他在南京路便衣执勤，清理主干道上的不良妇女，五名日本人中的四人向他发起攻击。

因 King 警长逮捕了几名妇女而感到愤怒，这五名日本人与该警官发生争执，随后其中四人对他实施殴打，第五人则试图安抚其同伴。

尽管那名未对警官动手的日本人的恳求，其他四人仍试图将 King 警长拖进一辆来自虹口车行、正等候他们的出租车，企图将 King 警长带至苏州河以北。

海福尔高地团士兵 Stevens 和工部局工务处督察 R. MacNeil 先生的及时介入干预了这场混战，使 King 警长免遭愤怒的日本人的伤害。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

DEC 15 1939

Japanese Assailants
Appear in Court
British Police Sergeant
Still in Hospital

Three of the four Japanese civilians arrested in Nanking Road on Wednesday evening following an assault on Police Sergeant M. King, British, while he was on duty there, appeared in the Japanese Consular Court yesterday morning. The fourth man had been released as it was found he had tried to prevent his companions from beating the police officer.

After a short hearing, the case was remanded until a future date when the injured police sergeant will be able to appear before the Court.

The three Japanese, with others who escaped, "ganged up" on Sergeant King as he was engaged in herding together some of the many Chinese prostitutes who nightly parade on Nanking Road in the vicinity of the large Chinese department stores. King was badly beaten and had to be sent to the Country Hospital where he will remain for some time.

1939年12月15日

日本袭击者
出庭受审
英国警长
仍在医院

周三晚在南京路袭击正在执勤的英国警长 M. King 后被捕的四名日本平民中的三人，于昨日上午出现在日本领事馆法庭。第四人被释放，因为发现他曾试图阻止同伴殴打警察。

经过简短听证，案件被延期审理，待受伤警长能够出庭时再定日期。

这三名日本人连同其他逃脱者，在 King 警长忙于驱赶每晚在南京路大型百货公司附近招摇过市的中国妓女时，“群起而攻之”。King 遭到严重殴打，被送往宏恩医院（Country Hospital），并将在那里停留一段时间。

Made by S.I. Barton. ....................Forwarded by........................................

Sir,

    I beg to report that at about 7.45 p.m. 13/10/38 whilst in
the station having dinner I was informed by F.S. Jack on Charge
Room duty that he had received a report that there was trouble
between Japanese and C.P.C. 1494 on Avenue Road near Park Road.
I immediately proceeded to the scene (outside 260 Avenue Road)
and found the C.P.C. standing in the middle of Avenue Road
surrounded by 4 male Japanese dressed in foreign clothing, he
was blowing his police whistle and had his pistol in his hand
(loaded). He informed me that he had been detailed to keep watch
on M/Truck Lic. No. 20475 loaded with scrap iron which have been
stopped for being overloaded pending the return of the driver.
He pointed to me one named M. Tsushiro Yashiro who he stated
had threatened him with a pistol and gestured me to get into a
private M/car Lic.No. 4537 which was stationary in front of the
truck. I requested all 4 Japanese to come to station (in English)
but by their attitude I could see that not one of them understood
me and all broke into laughter and split up in the middle of the
road wandering about in various directions. I kept keen observa-
tion on M. Tsushiro Yashiro until J.P.C. 243 (Gordon Road)
arrived on the scene to whom I reported the alleged report. All
4 Japanese were brought to the station at which time I left
F.S. Curtin and S.I. Chiang Ling Hsiang to watch the M/Truck and
the private M/Car. All 4 Japanese the M/Truck and the private
car and 5 male Chinese on the M/Truck were searched but no
pistol could be found.

                        I am, Sir,
                        Your obedient servant.

                                    Sun Inspector.

D.O. "B"

呈报人 副督察巴顿（Barton）____ 转呈人 ____ 

先生：

    谨此报告，1938年10月13日晚7时45分左右，我正在巡捕房内用晚餐时，值班室值班的警佐杰克（Jack）告知我，他接到报告称，在爱文义路（Avenue Road）近派克路（Park Road）处，有日本人与华捕第1494号发生纠纷。我立即赶赴现场（爱文义路260号外），发现该华捕站在爱文义路中央，被四名身穿西式服装的日本男子包围，他正在吹警哨，手中握着一把（已上膛的）手枪。他告诉我，他被指派看守一辆装载废铁的卡车（牌照号20475），该车因超载被拦停，等待司机返回。他指给我看其中一名叫矢代通四郎（M. Tsushiro Yashiro）的男子，称此人曾用手枪威胁他，并示意我坐进停在卡车前的一辆私人汽车（牌照号4537）。我用英语要求这四名日本人都到巡捕房去，但从他们的态度可以看出，他们中没有人听得懂我的话，他们都大笑起来，并在路中间散开，向各个方向游荡。我一直密切监视着矢代通四郎（M. Tsushiro Yashiro），直到戈登路（Gordon Road）的日捕第243号到达现场，我便向他报告了上述指控。随后，这四名日本人均被带至巡捕房，此时我留下警佐柯廷（Curtin）和副督察蒋灵祥（Chiang Ling Hsiang）看守那辆卡车和私人汽车。对这四名日本人、卡车、私人汽车以及卡车上的五名中国男子进行了搜查，但未发现手枪。

                        此致，
                        您顺从的仆人。

                                    孙督察。

“B”区值班警官

Between 3 and 7 p.m. 13/10/38, I was on duty at the corner of Avenue and Chengtu and at about 5.20 p.m. even date, I was giving signal which was in favour of North and South traffic when a motor truck proceeding West to East on Avenue Road which was travelling at a high speed. A girl age about 13 who tried to cross the roadway from North to South was almost knocked down but she was luckily seen and pulled by me to the south side of the road. At that time the truck was found to be loaded with scrap metal and the load was very high with five coolies sitting above the load and one of them was dozing. I told them that it was very dangerous to doze on the load when the vehicle was in motion when two men sitting by the side of the driver said that they would go to the station. I stood on the footboard and told the driver to drive east to the station. As the load was high, the truck was impossible to be driven into the station and therefore it stopped on Avenue Road near Kyburgh Road The two men sitting by the side of the driver alighted from the truck and went away and the driver told me that he would drive to their Headquarters. I tried to take him to the station but he refused, he only gave me his driving permit and went away towards the South along Park Road I reported the matter to the Charge Room where I handed this permit. This is my true statement.

1938年10月13日下午3时至7时之间，我在爱文义路与成都路拐角处执勤，同日约下午5时20分，我正在发出有利于南北向交通的信号，此时一辆卡车在爱文义路上由西向东高速行驶。一名约13岁的女孩试图由北向南横穿马路，险些被撞倒，但幸运的是被我看见并拉到了路南边。当时发现卡车上装载着废金属，货物堆得很高，有五名苦力坐在货物上面，其中一人正在打瞌睡。我告诉他们，车辆在行驶时在货物上打瞌睡是非常危险的，这时坐在司机旁边的两名男子说他们会去巡捕房。我站在踏脚板上，告诉司机向东开往巡捕房。由于货物太高，卡车无法驶入巡捕房，因此它停在爱文义路近基布赫路（Kyburgh Road）处。坐在司机旁边的两名男子下车离开，司机告诉我他将把车开到他们的总部。我试图带他去巡捕房，但他拒绝了，他只给了我他的驾驶执照，然后沿着派克路向南走去。我将此事报告给值班室，并移交了该执照。以上是我的真实陈述。

Between 7 and 11 p.m. 13/10/38 I was on duty at No. 8
Post, Avenue-Chengtu corner, and at about 7.45 p.m. even date
I was again detailed to guard an overloading private motor
truck No. 20475 loaded with scrap metal which was stationary
on Avenue Road near Park Road. I stood on the pavement on the
north side of the truck when four Japanese in civilian clothes
approached me and wanted to drive away the vehicle which I
stopped. They then surrounded me and as I was afraid that they
might rob me of my pistol I walked to the South side of the
truck and stood on the roadway. At that time C.P.C. 2586
walking 10 beat came along and I told him to report the matter to
the station. The four Japanese again followed me onto the
roadway and surrounded me when one of them took out a pistol
from his pocket and pointed same towards my chest while the
other three pushed me, intending to take me away into a
stationary private motor car No. 4537. For self-protection,
I took out my service pistol and worked my slide at the same
time I blew my whistle for assistance. S.I. Barton responded
and I pointed out to him the Japanese who was in possession of the
pistol. S.I. Barton then stood together with me. Afterwards
S.I. Chiang came to the scene and then F.S. 28 accompanied by
J.P.C. 43 also came. We then came to the station with the
Japanese and reported the matter to F.S. 358 on Charge Room duty.
This is my true statement.
(Sd) C.P.C. 1494

1938年9月29日上午10时，投诉人即莫里斯夫人
（因婚姻取得英国国籍者），系任职于公共卫生处（P.H.D.）的 J.D. 莫里斯先生之妻，前往威赛德巡捕房报案，称其遭到一名日本男子殴打。

后经侦探警员122号艾恩斯通（Eynstone）查询，查明
以下细节。

投诉人居住在西区，鉴于其丈夫的职责要求他留在苏州河以北，该住所对其丈夫不便，莫里斯夫妇决定设法在苏州河以北寻找合适的住房。

为此目的，1938年9月29日上午9时10分左右，莫里斯夫人在外白渡桥附近登上了一辆公共汽车，这是目前由日本人运营的众多车辆之一。

随后的行程导致莫里斯夫人遭到殴打，以下细节与本人从投诉人处获取的陈述一致：-

“1938年9月29日上午9时10分左右，我在外白渡桥附近登上了一辆公共汽车，涉事车辆是苏州河以北由日本人运营的车辆之一，车牌号或可能的识别号码我不知晓。

1938年9月29日上午9时30分左右，公共汽车停在百老汇路（Broadway East）靠近穆黑德路（Muirhead Road）处，我打算在此下车。

然而在下车之前，我递给日本售票员一枚20分的银币，同时问他车费是多少，他用外语（可能是日语）回答，因此鉴于这一困难，我问了公共汽车司机，希望他会说英语。

然而售票员拒绝找给我2分钱，于是我和其他几名乘客连同售票员一起下了车。
下了公共汽车后，日本售票员用外语说了些什么，然后推了我，并用手掌多次扇我的耳光。
鉴于这次无端袭击，我试图逮捕袭击者，打算将他移交警方拘留。
然而售票员进行反抗，双手掐住我的脖子，并将我的头撞向墙壁。
几秒钟后，售票员松开了掐住我脖子的手，随后登上车辆，车辆立即向东驶离。
随后我前往威赛德巡捕房报告了这一事件。

“我以贩卖通心粉为业，居住在穆黑德路45号。
1933年9月29日上午9时30分左右，当我站在百老汇路北侧靠近穆黑德路处时，我看见一辆公共汽车（类似于苏州河以北运行且由日本人运营的那些）停在百老汇路北侧

East near Muirhead Road, the bus was numbered 20.
A number of passengers alighted, and at this time I observed the Japanese conductor (who incidently had also alighted from the vehicle) shout at a foreign female then slap her on the face with his hands several times.
It then appeared that the foreign female attempted to apprehend her assailant whereupon the latter placed both his hands around her neck and banged her head against a wall.
After the lapse of a few seconds the Japanese conductor relinquished his hold on her neck, then boarded the bus which immediately drove away in an easterly direction.
At about 11.20 a.m. 23-9-38 Chinese and a foreign detective made enquiries at the scene of the offence and having questioned me and ascertained that I witnessed the incident they requested me to visit Wayside Police Station where I voluntarily made this statement."
With the assistance of J.D.C. 157 namely Hanawa a full report was made to the Japanese Consular Police who were handed a Japanese translation of the statement made by Mrs. Morris, they promising to conduct immediate enquiries and take the necessary action against the culprit.
At the time of writing this report the investigating detective is waiting for further information from the Consular Police regarding the results of their enquiries and action to be taken.
The complainant was escorted to the Shanghai General Hospital where Dr. Patrick issued the following medical certificate:-
"Mrs. Morris, Lane 1355/No.18 Ta Yuen Road seen at Hospital 11.45 a.m. on account of personal injury from assault.
Slight marking on neck and face as from throttling and slapping - No serious injury."
Enquiries proceeding.

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS

SEP 30 1938

Japanese Strikes
British Woman

Mrs. J. D. Morris Beaten
By Bus Conductor After
Argument Over Fare

A British woman was yesterday morning so badly beaten by a Japanese bus conductor that she had to be taken to the General Hospital and treated for injuries to the head and body.

The woman, Mrs. J. D. Morris, of House 12-A, Lane 1355 Yu Yuen Road, had boarded a Japanese bus outside the Broadway Mansions at 9.10 o'clock in order to go to Broadway East and Muirhead Road. Near her destination she asked the Japanese conductor what the fare was. He apparently did not understand English, and she asked the Japanese driver. The latter, according to Mrs. Morris, said the fare was 10 cents. She gave the conductor 20 cents, she said, but received only 8 cents change. She protested and then alighted from the bus.

The conductor followed her to the street, Mrs. Morris later reported to the Settlement Police. There, she said, he slapped her face, pushed her in the chest, grabbed her by the neck and finally bumped her against a wall. After this treatment the conductor left her, stunned, in the roadway, boarded his bus and rode off in it. She made an unsuccessful attempt to hold him till help arrived. But when the police came from Wayside Station the bus was already out of sight.

Mrs. Morris was taken to the General Hospital in a motor-car and treated for her injuries. Her condition was not considered to be serious.

It is understood that the incident was reported by the Settlement Police to the Japanese Consular Police. British Consular authorities also are investigating.

The number of the Japanese bus involved was 20, witnesses told the investigators.

Another Woman Assaulted

At 4.25 p.m., Mrs. O. V. Pachnina, Russian, of House 6, Lane 125 Wayside Road, alighted from Japanese Bus No. 43 at a stop near her home. Along with her, many other passengers got out, and also the conductor.

The conductor, according to reports later made to the police, started an argument with Mrs. Pachnina as to whether she had paid her fare. She had, but apparently some other woman passenger had not.

"Are you English?" the conductor suddenly asked Mrs. Pachnina.

"Yes," she answered, for some unknown reason.

The conductor immediately kicked and pushed her, then boarded his bus and vanished with it.

Mrs. Pachnina reported the assault to Wayside Station detectives within twenty minutes of its occurrence.

《字林西报》

1938年9月30日

日本人殴打
英国妇女

J. D. 莫里斯夫人在车费争执后
被公交车售票员殴打

一名英国妇女昨天早晨遭到一名日本公交车售票员的严重殴打，以致不得不被送往总医院接受头部和身体受伤的治疗。

这名妇女是 J. D. 莫里斯夫人，住在愚园路1355弄12-A号，她于9点10分在百老汇大厦（Broadway Mansions，即上海大厦）外登上了一辆日本公交车，打算前往百老汇路和缪尔黑德路。在接近目的地时，她问日本售票员车费是多少。他显然听不懂英语，于是她问了日本司机。据莫里斯夫人称，后者说车费是10分。她说她给了售票员20分，但只找回8分。她提出抗议，然后下了车。

莫里斯夫人后来向租界警方报告说，售票员跟着她到了街上。她说，在那里，他扇了她的耳光，推了她的胸口，掐住她的脖子，最后把她撞向墙壁。经过这番折磨后，售票员将她神志不清地留在马路上，登上他的公交车开车离去。她试图拦住他直到救援到来，但未成功。但当警察从韦斯特盖特巡捕房（Wayside Station，即小沙渡巡捕房）赶来时，公交车已不见踪影。

莫里斯夫人被汽车送往总医院治疗伤势。她的情况被认为并不严重。

据悉，租界警方已将此事件报告给日本领事警察。英国领事当局也在进行调查。

目击者告诉调查人员，涉案的日本公交车编号为20号。

另一名妇女遭袭击

下午4点25分，俄罗斯籍的 O. V. Pachnina（音译）夫人，住在韦斯特盖特路（Wayside Road，即小沙渡路）125弄6号，在离家不远的一个车站从日本43路公交车上下来。和她一起下车的还有许多其他乘客，售票员也下了车。

据后来向警方提交的报告称，售票员就帕赫尼娜（Pachnina）夫人是否支付了车费一事与她发生了争执。她付了，但显然有其他女乘客未付。

“你是英国人吗？”售票员突然问帕赫尼娜夫人。

“是的，”她出于某种未知原因回答道。

售票员立即踢打并推搡她，然后登上公交车，随车消失。

帕赫尼娜夫人在袭击发生后二十分钟内向韦斯特盖特巡捕房（Wayside Station，即小沙渡巡捕房）的侦探报告了此次袭击。

Between 8p.m. and 12m.n. 21/8/38 I was posted for duty

who was standing outside the church, whereupon P.S. 141
approached the Japanese and questioned him regarding the

At 10.50a.m. even date, whilst the traffic signals were allowing vehicles to pass from North to South I observed a Japanese standing in the roadway at the foot of the bridge calling for a public ricsha. I then informed him that as he had assaulted me and interfered with the lawful discharge of my duty, that he should accompany me to the Police Station. This resulted in his seizing my cross belt with his right hand and asking me to go to the Japanese Military Headquarters in Hongkew. My name is Toshi Isono (磯野寿), dentist, residing at Lane
332 House 34 Woosung Road.
I intended to buy some materials for dental operation in the
area South of Creek and crossed over Garden Bridge N. to S.
at about 11a.m. and wished to hire ricsha at the south end of
the bridge.
Two or three ricshas approached me in response to my call
and I took one of them and was about to ride on when C.P.C. 1807
came to us and suddenly took away the puller's arm badge No. 33116
from the puller. On seeing this, I explained in local dialect
that I hired the ricsha and begged the constable not to seize the
badge, when the C.P.C., patting his service pistol on his waist,
took such a threatening attitude that he would arrest me if I
dared to press the matter further.
After a few words which I could not understand, the C.P.C.
hold me on the coat and tried to take me to somewhere in South-
ern direction, so I shook my body to release his tight holding
of my coat, but I have no knowledge of the constable's lanyard /being
torn up.
In the meantime, Japanese police man came to the scene and I
and the constable were both taken to this station.
This is my true statement.

(Signed).
磯野 寿
31/8/38

我打算去苏州河以南地区购买一些牙科手术材料，约于上午11时由北向南穿过外白渡桥，并希望在桥南端雇用人力车。
两三个人力车响应我的呼唤向我靠近，我乘坐了其中一辆，正欲上车时，华捕第1807号来到我们面前，突然从车夫手臂上取走第33116号拉车牌。见此情形，我用本地方言解释说我已雇用该车，并恳请巡捕不要没收号牌，此时该华捕拍打着腰间的佩枪，摆出威胁姿态，称若我再纠缠此事便将逮捕我。

At 10.45a.m. I was leaving Garden Bridge, after visiting
the sentries posted there. I was on the point of entering my
car which was 40 yards south of the bridge on the East side,
when I observed a Japanese in civilian clothes struggling with
and striking a Chinese Constable of the S.M.P. He was
apparently attempting to take from the constable a metal disc,
which was later identified as a rickshaw coolie's license.
He struck the constable several times and tore his revolver
lanyard. At that moment a Foreign Sergeant of the S.M.P., who
was on duty on the Garden Bridge came down and attempted to
pacify the Japanese. The Japanese attempted to strike the
Foreign Sergeant, but his blows fell considerably short of the
mark. I enquired of the Foreign Sergt if he required any
assistance. He replied he would like a man to guard the
Japanese, whilst he telephoned. I fetched the Corporal on
duty (Corporal Young) from the bridge, who guarded the Japanese
while the phone call to the Central Police Station was put
through.

CER 1 1930

Japanese Attacks
Traffic Constable

Hongkew Dentist Seized
After Causing Trouble
At Garden Bridge

A Japanese civilian who gave his name as T. Isono and said he was a dentist in Hongkew created a disturbance at the south end of the Garden Bridge yesterday morning when he tried to prevent a traffic policeman from carrying out his duties.

The incident occurred at about 10.40 o'clock and was witnessed by several foreigners. At that time a Chinese constable who had been placed near the bridge to deal with "wild" rickshaws saw a puller violate the Municipal regulations by dashing up the approach to the bridge despite the constable's efforts to restrain him. The elusive puller in fact managed to pick up a Japanese passenger and then tried to return with his fare past the policeman.

The constable, however, proceeded to carry out his instructions and halted the rickshaw, at the same time demanding the puller's arm-badge. At this point the Japanese passenger, Isono, protested and as the policeman endeavoured to take the badge from the puller's arm the Japanese descended from the rickshaw and, in the presence of scores of witnesses, struck the constable in the chest.

Not satisfied with hitting the policeman, the Japanese, according to reports made to Central Police Station, further grasped his belt and pistol "lanyard" and started to pull the C.P.C. up the bridge towards the Hongkew side.

At this juncture the foreign police sergeant on duty at Soochow Road and the bridge arrived on the scene and attempted to pacify the Japanese. The latter, however, would not be pacified and even struck at the much bigger foreigner. The blows made no impression on the massively-built sergeant.

A lieutenant in the Seaforth Highlanders appeared on the scene at this moment and asked if he could give assistance to the police. The foreign sergeant asked the lieutenant if he could provide someone to look after the Japanese while he, the sergeant, telephoned to Central Station. The lieutenant quickly summoned a corporal from the guard stationed at the British Consulate-General.

Some five minutes later the Japanese trouble-maker and the two policemen were on their way to the station, from where a call was sent to the Japanese Consular Police. The Japanese was handed over to Consular constables. It was said that action will be taken against him in the Japanese Consular Court.

The Chinese constable had to be sent to the Police Hospital for treatment of bruises on his chest and abrasions on his left hand.

CER 1 1930

日本人袭击
交通巡捕

虹口牙医制造麻烦后
在外白渡桥被捕

一名自称T. Isono、称自己是虹口牙医的日本平民，昨天上午在外白渡桥南端试图阻止交通巡捕执行职务，从而引发骚乱。

事件发生在约10时40分，数名外国人目睹了经过。当时，一名被部署在桥附近以处理“野鸡”人力车的华捕，看到一名车夫无视巡捕的制止，违反市政规定冲上桥引道。这名难以捉摸的车夫实际上成功载上了一名日本乘客，然后试图载着客人从巡捕身边经过返回。

然而，巡捕继续执行指令，拦停人力车，同时要求车夫交出臂章。此时，日本乘客矶野提出抗议，当巡捕试图从车夫手臂上取下号牌时，该日本人从人力车上下来，在众多目击者面前击打巡捕胸部。

据向中央捕房提交的报告称，该日本人并不满足于殴打警察，还进一步抓住其腰带和手枪“挂绳”，并开始将华捕沿桥向虹口方向拖拽。

此时，在苏州路和外白渡桥执勤的外籍巡长赶到现场，试图平息该日本人的情绪。然而，后者不肯罢休，甚至击打身材比他高大得多的外国人。这些拳头对这位体格魁梧的巡长毫无影响。

此刻，苏格兰海福特高地团的一名中尉出现在现场，询问是否可以向警方提供协助。外籍巡长问该中尉能否派人照看该日本人，以便他（巡长）打电话给中央捕房。中尉迅速召来驻扎在英国总领事馆的警卫队中的一名下士。

大约五分钟后，这名制造麻烦的日本人及两名警察启程前往捕房，并从那里致电日本领事馆警察。该日本人被移交给领事馆巡捕。据悉，日本领事馆法庭将对他采取行动。

该名华捕因胸部挫伤和左手擦伤，被送往警察医院接受治疗。
